G37:1: To set apart for God, dedicate, make ritually clean, or declare holy.
G37:2: To honor and revere God's name as holy.
G37:3: To separate believers from sin and make them holy; the state of having been made holy.
G59:1: To buy something by paying a price.
G59:2: To buy a person by paying a price; to redeem.
G68:1: A field where crops grow, open country where grass and flowers grow, and the place where one works in the field.
G68:2: The countryside outside towns and villages.
G68:3: Land or farmland that is bought, sold, owned, or transferred.
G91:1: To do wrong or treat someone unjustly; to cause harm; to do evil.
G91:3: To harm people or creatures (grass, trees, the earth, the sea).
G169:1: πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον: a description of the evil spirit that takes hold of a person.
G169:2: What is unclean under the law or ritually (foods, animals, people).
G169:3: Sexual or moral impurity; people or deeds marked by it.
G227:1: Words, testimony, or matters that accord with the facts and contain no falsehood.
G227:2: A person, or God, who is without falsehood and speaks the truth.
G228:1: Genuine, real, as opposed to a shadow or imitation.
G228:2: Words, testimony, or a way that is true and without falsehood.

G268:1: One named a "sinner" by those around, often listed with τελῶναι; said of those with whom Jesus keeps company, or as the judgment of some.

G314:1: To read a document, Scripture, or a letter; to read for oneself and understand.
G314:2: To read aloud before an assembly; to be read aloud (in worship or gatherings).
G386:1: The raising of the dead. ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν (resurrection of the dead), ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει (at the resurrection), ἀνάστασις ζωῆς／κρίσεως, ἡ ἀνάστασις ἡ πρώτη, and so on.

G417:1: A wind of nature, a storm, the blowing of a gale.
G417:2: The four winds, that is, east, west, south, and north; the four quarters of the earth.
G417:3: A figure for teaching as a wind that shakes people and tosses them about.
G514:1: A person or thing deserving some matter or treatment, having the fitting standing or worth: ἄξιος λαβεῖν, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος ἵνα λύσω, ἄξιος ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ, πάσης ἀποδοχῆς ἄξιος, etc.

G514:3: States the punishment or retribution that is due: θανάτου ἄξιον (deserving death), ἄξια πληγῶν, ἄξια ὧν ἐπράξαμεν, etc.
G518:1: To tell and report to someone what has happened or been seen or heard. Most uses are messengers or eyewitnesses reporting what they saw or what occurred.

G537:1: Modifies a noun to mean "whole" or "all".
G537:2: Used as a noun for all the people, everyone.
G537:3: In the neuter, refers to all matters or things as a whole.
G591:1: To give back, pay, or render to another what is rightly due: a debt, wages, or something owed.
G591:2: To give a reward, payment, or return according to what someone has done. Used for good and for evil ("repay evil with evil").

G591:4: To hand over or return an object or person to its original owner or the one in charge.
G591:5: In the middle voice ἀποδίδομαι: to sell off an object or person.
G591:6: To produce or give forth fruit, testimony, and the like.
G601:1: God or the Son shows and makes known to people what was hidden.
G601:2: Hidden thoughts or deeds are brought out into the open.
G601:3: At the end time, Christ, glory, the lawless one, and others appear.
G680:1: To touch an object or person with the hand (middle ἅπτομαι): Jesus touching to heal, touching the tassel of a garment, children being touched, etc.
G680:2: To meddle with what is forbidden or unclean, or to harm someone; also to touch a woman (euphemism): ἀκαθάρτου μὴ ἅπτεσθε, μὴ ἅψῃ μηδὲ γεύσῃ, οὐχ ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ (the evil one does not touch him), γυναικὸς μὴ ἅπτεσθαι.
G680:3: To light a lamp or fire: λύχνον ἅψας, ἅπτει λύχνον, ἅψαντες πυράν.
G720:1: To deny a fact or a relationship; to say "I do not know"; to disown.
G720:2: To disown Christ, God, the faith, or the sovereign; to turn away; to reject the truth.
G720:3: To deny oneself, renounce desires, decline a position or a name.
G721:1: The lamb as the title of Christ in Revelation.
G721:2: A lamb as an animal; a figure for a flock of sheep (the disciples).
G737:1: An adverb marking the present moment of speaking: "now doing", "now is…".
G737:2: In the form ἀπ᾽ ἄρτι, points forward from this moment onward.
G737:3: In the forms ἕως ἄρτι and ἄχρι τῆς ἄρτι ὥρας, marks continuation from the past up to now.
G737:4: Marks something that has only just happened.
G758:1: A human ruler or leader: Jewish councillors and leaders (οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν Ἰουδαίων), the synagogue ruler (ἄρχων τῆς συναγωγῆς), Gentile rulers, officials, heads of a people, and so on.
G758:2: The ruler of demons (ὁ ἄρχων τῶν δαιμονίων), the ruler of this world (ὁ ἄρχων τοῦ κόσμου τούτου), the ruler of the authority of the air (Eph 2:2).
G770:1: To suffer from bodily illness; to be sick.
G770:2: To lack strength, faith, or conscience; to bear weakness.
G772:1: One who is sick; a sick person.
G772:2: Lacking strength: a weak body, flesh, person, or law; those who are weak.
G772:3: A person whose conscience or faith is weak.
G891:1: A preposition with the genitive marking an end point in time. Appears in forms such as "until this day" and "until the end".
G891:2: A conjunctive use, with a clause following οὗ, ἧς ἡμέρας and the like: until the time when something happens.
G891:3: A preposition marking the end point of place, or the limit of degree ("even to death").
G941:1: To lift up and carry a thing or person; to shoulder; to support.
G941:2: To carry, bear, or endure a burden, a weakness, or a charge.
G941:3: To carry a name or a mark on one's body.
G975:1: A written scroll or book, a document; includes scrolls of Scripture, letters, and sealed scrolls.
G975:3: The book of life, the heavenly record in which people's deeds are written.
G987:1: To utter words that defile what is holy: God, the Holy Spirit, God's name, God's word, teaching.
G987:2: To speak maliciously of, or insult, a person (including Jesus), a glorious being, or a person's deeds or teaching.
G1014:1: A person wants, intends, or wishes to do something: ἐβουλόμην πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν, βούλεσθε ἀπολύσω (shall I release…?), ἐβούλετο συμπαραλαβεῖν, οἱ βουλόμενοι πλουτεῖν, etc.
G1014:2: Used of the will or decision of God or Christ: καθὼς βούλεται (the Spirit), μὴ βουλόμενός τινας ἀπολέσθαι, βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς, ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ υἱός, εἰ βούλει παρένεγκε (Luke 22:42).
G1014:3: In the form βούλομαι + infinitive / accusative with infinitive, the writer states their own wish or instruction: βούλομαι οὖν προσεύχεσθαι τοὺς ἄνδρας, γινώσκειν ὑμᾶς βούλομαι, περὶ τούτων βούλομαί σε διαβεβαιοῦσθαι.
G1060:1: For a man to take a wife, for a woman to be given in marriage, to become husband and wife.
G1060:2: In contexts of marrying a divorced person, or of divorcing and marrying another.
G1074:1: The people living in a given age; used for the people of that time as a whole, such as "this generation" or "an unbelieving and twisted generation".
G1074:2: A division of generations or successive generations: "fourteen generations", "from generation to generation", "past generations", "all generations", etc.
G1100:1: The tongue as a bodily organ in the mouth.
G1100:2: The tongue as the seat of speaking, declaring, confessing, or deceiving; speech itself expressed by the tongue.
G1100:3: The language people use, and the name of a people distinguished by it; listed with φυλή, λαός, ἔθνος.
G1100:4: Linked with λαλεῖν／προσεύχεσθαι, speech spoken of as a gift of the Spirit in 1 Cor 12–14 and elsewhere; paired with ἑρμηνεία.
G1100:5: In the Pentecost scene, tongue-shaped things that appeared divided like fire.
G1108:1: Knowledge about God, Christ, and salvation; also the knowing of that knowledge.
G1108:2: Knowledge held by believers, knowledge as a gift of the Spirit, knowledge as one of the virtues.
G1124:1: With the definite article, ἡ γραφή or αἱ γραφαί refers to what is written, that is, Scripture. Appears in "Scripture says", "Scripture is fulfilled", "read / search the Scriptures", and may mean either a quotation from a particular passage or Scripture in general.
G1124:2: With a demonstrative, ἑτέρα, ἐν γραφῇ and the like, singles out one passage of Scripture.
G1124:3: Without the article and with a modifier, speaks of a "sacred writing".
G1166:1: To show a visible object, a place, a part of the body, and the like; to point out.
G1166:2: God, an angel, or another being shows and makes known through a vision, a revelation, or teaching.
G1166:3: To show evidence or prove by signs or deeds.
G1208:1: What comes next after the first in an order or list: "the second man", "the second commandment", "the second tent", "the second angel", etc.
G1208:2: The same thing happening once more. In the forms ἐκ δευτέρου and τὸ δεύτερον, an adverbial use meaning "a second time" or "again".
G1208:3: The set expression "the second death". In Revelation it refers to being thrown into the lake of fire.
G1210:1: To bind and tie things, animals, bundles, bodies, and the like with cords or cloth: "the donkey is tied", "bind the weeds in bundles", "wrap in linen", etc.
G1210:2: To bind a person with ropes or chains and hold them. Appears in scenes of arrest, being led away, and imprisonment.
G1210:3: A person held and bound by law, marriage, the Spirit's leading, and the like.
G1210:4: To bind demons, Satan, angels, and other beings beyond human; also the state of being bound.
G1210:5: "Whatever you bind on earth is bound in heaven": a use stated in pair with "binding and loosing".
G1228:1: A noun for the one who opposes God and tempts and accuses people. ὁ διάβολος (the tempter in the wilderness, the one bound at the end of the age, ἀντίδικος ὑμῶν), τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου, τέκνα τοῦ διαβόλου, ὁ ἀρχαῖος ὄφις ὁ καλούμενος Διάβολος καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς, etc.
G1228:2: As an adjective or noun, one who slanders or gossips about people: γυναῖκας σεμνὰς μὴ διαβόλους (1 Tim 3:11), διάβολοι (2 Tim 3:3), μὴ διαβόλους (Titus 2:3).
G1242:1: A covenant made between God and people (with Abraham, at Sinai, the new covenant, etc.), and the sign of that covenant or its ark.
G1242:2: The will of a person who has died (Heb 9:16–17).
G1247:1: To wait at table and care for personal needs: ἡ Μάρθα διηκόνει, πυρετός ... διηκόνει αὐτοῖς, ἄγγελοι διηκόνουν αὐτῷ, γυναῖκες ἠκολούθουν καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ, ὁ διακονῶν (Luke 22:26–27), διακονεῖν τραπέζαις, etc.
G1247:2: To serve and carry out a service for people, Christ, or the saints: οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι (Matt 20:28), ἐμοί τις διακονῇ (John 12:26), διακονήσαντες τοῖς ἁγίοις, οἱ καλῶς διακονήσαντες (1 Tim 3:13), χάρισμα ... διακονοῦντες, etc.
G1247:3: To handle as a task the collecting and carrying of relief funds, the writing of a letter, and the like: τῇ χάριτι ταύτῃ τῇ διακονουμένῃ ὑφ᾽ ἡμῶν, ἐπιστολὴ Χριστοῦ διακονηθεῖσα ὑφ᾽ ἡμῶν, πορεύομαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ διακονῶν τοῖς ἁγίοις.
G1248:1: A service given by God or the Lord: service in the church, the work of the gospel and of the word, service as a spiritual gift.
G1248:2: Close care and serving, such as caring for meals and daily distribution.
G1248:3: Aid for the saints in Jerusalem; the service of bringing the collection.
G1249:1: One who serves a master or king; a table attendant; any servant.
G1249:2: A worker who serves the gospel, the church, or the Lord; a missionary.
G1249:3: A service office appointed in the church; deacon.
G1249:4: A ruler who acts on God's authority.
G1322:1: What is taught: content, doctrine, a body of teaching.
G1322:2: The act of teaching by Jesus, the apostles, and others; the scene of teaching ("astonished at the teaching", "in his teaching").
G1330:1: Passing through a place, object, or person to the other side: διὰ μέσον Σαμαρείας, διὰ τῆς θαλάσσης, διὰ τρυμαλιᾶς ῥαφίδος, διὰ τῶν οὐρανῶν, ῥομφαία διελεύσεται, etc.
G1330:2: Going from one region or town to the next: διῆλθον τὴν Φρυγίαν, διήρχοντο κατὰ τὰς κώμας, διερχόμενος εὐηγγελίζετο τὰς πόλεις, etc.
G1330:3: Going or crossing over toward a destination marked by εἰς／ἕως and the like: Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν, Διέλθωμεν ἕως Βηθλέεμ, διελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν, etc.
G1330:4: A report or death spreading and reaching among people: διήρχετο ὁ λόγος, ὁ θάνατος διῆλθεν εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους.
G1344:1: God pronounces a person righteous, and the person is made righteous by that pronouncement. Spoken of in relation to faith, works of the law, the blood of Christ, and grace.
G1344:2: People recognize God or wisdom as right, people try to show themselves right, or the rightness of God or wisdom is shown (by words spoken or deeds done).
G1377:1: To pursue, harass, and attack people. Appears where prophets, Jesus, disciples, and the church are persecuted, and in the passive "to be persecuted".
G1377:2: To strive toward good things: virtue, peace, righteousness, love, a goal.
G1377:3: To go to a place in pursuit of a person.
G1398:1: To serve as a slave or servant, to submit to a master one ought to serve; also the subjection of a nation or people.
G1398:2: To serve and minister to the Lord, God, or Christ.
G1398:3: To be bound as a slave under sin, desire, worldly powers, or the law.
G1398:4: To serve one another in love.
G1415:1: A person with strength, ability, or influence; also a powerful means.
G1415:2: A matter is possible and can happen (εἰ δυνατόν, πάντα δυνατά).
G1415:3: A person or God has the ability to do something (+ infinitive).
G1448:1: Drawing near spatially to a person, place, or thing: ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ, ἐγγίζων τῇ Δαμασκῷ, ἤγγισεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ, ὁ παραδιδούς ἤγγικεν, etc.

G1448:3: A time, day, event, or something coming draws close: ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία, ἤγγικεν ὁ καιρός／ἡ ὥρα／ἡ ἡμέρα／τὸ τέλος, etc.
G1451:2: Near in time; a time is at hand (a feast, a season, the end).
G1451:3: Near in relationship or state; in a state close to becoming so.
G1564:1: Away from that place. The starting point of a movement.
G1564:2: In the form ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ("on this side and on that"), one of the two sides.
G1607:1: People, spirits, or groups go out of a place, depart, come out.
G1607:2: Words, thoughts, a sword, fire, and the like come out of or are sent out from the mouth, heart, or body.
G1607:3: Lightning, a river, or the Spirit proceeds from a source such as the throne or the Father; a report spreads.
G1632:1: To pour out, spill, or scatter liquid or objects; to be spilled.
G1632:2: To shed blood; for blood to be shed.
G1632:3: To pour out the Spirit, love, wrath, and the like upon people. Includes the pouring out of the bowls in Revelation.
G1632:4: (Figurative) To give oneself wholly over to error, desire, and the like; to throw oneself into it.
G1653:1: A person or God shows mercy and compassion to one who suffers.
G1653:2: To be shown mercy; to become one who has received mercy (passive).
G1653:3: An imperative cry asking for help, as in Κύριε ἐλέησον.
G1656:1: Mercy and loving-kindness that God shows to people.
G1656:2: Mercy and compassion that one person shows another.
G1656:3: A word of greeting and prayer, listed with "grace" and "peace" ("grace, mercy, and peace").
G1679:1: To hope for what is future, to have expectations, to expect that…
G1679:2: To set one's hope on an object such as God or Christ and rely on them (ἐπί／εἰς + object).
G1683:1: The first-person reflexive pronoun, referring to the subject itself: ἐμαυτὸν ἐδούλωσα, περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ μαρτυρῶ, οὐδὲν ἐμαυτῷ σύνοιδα, πρὸς ἐμαυτὸν (to myself), etc.
G1683:2: In the forms ἀπ᾽ ἐμαυτοῦ／ἐξ ἐμαυτοῦ, says that one acts, or does not act, on one's own judgment and authority (in John's Gospel).
G1715:1: A preposition (with the genitive) for "before the eyes of" a person, God, or a court, or where witnesses, hearers, or judges are present. Appears in scenes of confession, denial, glory, and judgment.
G1715:2: A preposition (with the genitive) for physical position, "in front of" or "ahead of".
G1715:3: Without a genitive, as an adverb meaning "ahead" or "to the front".
G1715:4: Higher in rank than another. In John's Gospel, used by John the Baptist of Jesus, who comes after him; accompanied by the reason, "because he was before me".
G1746:1: To put on or dress in clothing.
G1746:2: To put on virtue, Christ, armor, strength, immortality, and the like, as one puts on clothing.
G1832:1: Permitted, or not permitted, by the law, a regulation, or a statute (the Sabbath, divorce, paying tax, etc.).
G1832:2: Allowed to do something as an individual; having the freedom or room to do it.
G1893:1: A conjunction giving reason or ground: "because", "since".
G1893:2: "Otherwise": introduces the unwelcome consequence that would follow if the previous matter were denied.
G1921:1: To recognize who or what a person or thing is, by seeing or hearing; to identify something familiar.
G1921:2: To become aware, by seeing or being told, of an event, a situation, or another person's thoughts; to realize a fact from an immediate observation or report.
G1921:3: To know an object (truth, God's grace, a person, etc.) clearly and with certainty; a use in which completeness and certainty are added to "knowing" (γινώσκω).
G1921:4: To establish the circumstances, reason, or facts by questioning or investigation.
G1921:5: To recognize a person or a teaching as something to be accepted.
G1939:1: Fleshly or worldly desire, covetousness: ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σαρκός, ἐπιθυμίαι κοσμικαί, κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας πορεύεσθαι, ἐπιθυμία ἀπὸ τῆς ἰδίας (Jas 1:14), τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν οὐκ ᾔδειν (Rom 7:7), etc.
G1939:2: Strong wishing and longing, including in a good sense: ἐν πολλῇ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἰδεῖν (1 Thess 2:17), ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἐπεθύμησα (Luke 22:15), τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν ἔχων εἰς τὸ ἀναλῦσαι (Phil 1:23), τῆς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς ψυχῆς (Rev 18:14).
G1941:1: To be called by a name, to be given a nickname, to have a name attached.
G1941:2: To call on the name of God, the Lord, or the Father in prayer and worship.
G1941:3: To appeal to a higher authority.
G1941:4: To call God as witness to one's own words.
G1994:1: To turn the body or face around: to look back, to turn toward a voice or a person.
G1994:2: To go back, or be brought back, to the original place, owner, or state.
G1994:3: To turn one's heart back to God or the Lord and change one's way of living (intransitive and passive forms).
G1994:4: To turn a person back toward God or the right way, to bring them back (transitive).
G2007:1: To place or lay an object on something: ἐπέθηκαν ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια, ἐπιτίθησιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους, στέφανον ἐπέθηκαν, πηλὸν ἐπέθηκεν, etc.
G2007:2: In the form ἐπιτίθημι τὰς χεῖρας, to lay hands on someone for healing, blessing, appointment, or giving the Holy Spirit.
G2007:3: To lay a burden, load, blow, or calamity on another: ζυγὸν／βάρος ἐπιτιθέναι, πληγὰς ἐπιτιθέναι, τὸν σταυρὸν ἐπέθηκαν, ἐπιθήσει ὁ θεὸς τὰς πληγάς.
G2007:4: To add something to a book (Rev 22:18).
G2007:5: In the form ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα, to give a person a name (Peter, Boanerges).
G2007:6: In the middle voice, to launch an attack against a person: οὐδεὶς ἐπιθήσεταί σοι τοῦ κακῶσαί σε.
G2008:1: To scold, sternly warn, or censure a person.
G2008:2: To rebuke evil spirits, wind, fever, and the like, calming them and making them obey.
G2008:3: To sternly warn someone to keep something secret.
G2038:1: To engage in work and labor: ἐργάζεσθαι ταῖς χερσίν, νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας ἐργαζόμενοι, εἰ τις οὐ θέλει ἐργάζεσθαι, ὁ ἐργαζόμενος (the one who works), etc.
G2038:2: To actually do an act, a work, good or evil: ἐργάζεσθαι τὸ ἀγαθόν, ἔργον καλὸν ἐργάζεσθαι, τὰ ἔργα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐργάζεσθαι, δικαιοσύνην／ἀνομίαν ἐργάζεσθαι, etc.
G2038:3: In 2 Cor 7:10, ἡ λύπη … μετάνοιαν ἐργάζεται: one thing produces or brings about a result.
G2048:1: As ἡ ἔρημος, a noun for the wide uninhabited country. Appears in scenes such as the Baptist's preaching, Jesus' temptation, and Israel's wilderness journey.
G2048:2: An adjective modifying τόπος and the like, describing a place with no people.
G2048:3: Said of a house, dwelling, or woman: in a state of desolation, with no one living there.
G2090:1: To get ready beforehand what is needed: a meal, the Passover, a place, lodging, equipment: τόπον ἑτοιμάσαι, τὸ πάσχα ἑτοιμάζειν, ἀρώματα ἡτοίμασαν, ξενίαν ἑτοίμαζε, etc.

G2090:3: In the forms ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου and ἑτοιμάσαι κυρίῳ λαὸν, to make ready the way or the people for the Lord's coming.
G2090:4: In the form ἑτοιμάζω ἑαυτόν, to make preparations oneself.
G2094:1: A year as a length of time. Combined with numerals, it is used in the forms "for … years", "… years ago", "for … years now".
G2094:2: States a person's age by the genitive ἐτῶν with a numeral.
G2094:3: Refers to a particular year in the calendar, or to yearly repetition with κατ᾽ ἔτος.
G2112:1: An adverb showing that something follows immediately, without a gap, after the preceding event or action.
G2112:2: Shows that something will happen in the near future.
G2127:1: To pronounce a blessing on a person, or to grant favor; also, in the passive, to receive that blessing: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς διώκοντας, ὁ εὐλογήσας ἡμᾶς, εὐλογεῖσθαι, etc.
G2127:2: To praise God, with God as the object: εὐλογῶν τὸν θεόν, εὐλογοῦμεν τὸν κύριον καὶ πατέρα.
G2127:3: In the passive perfect participle εὐλογημένος／η／οι, a form for saying or calling out that a person is "blessed": "εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου", etc.
G2127:4: Used with εὐλογεῖν before bread, fish, or a cup: εὐλογήσας ἔκλασεν, τὸ ποτήριον ὃ εὐλογοῦμεν, etc.
G2168:1: To give thanks to God or people: εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν (letter openings), εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι (John 11:41, Luke 18:11), ἐν παντὶ εὐχαριστεῖτε, εὐχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν, etc.
G2168:2: To take bread or a cup and offer a prayer of thanks: λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν, ποτήριον εὐχαριστήσας, ὁ ἐσθίων κυρίῳ ἐσθίει εὐχαριστεῖ γὰρ τῷ θεῷ.
G2190:1: One who is hostile, a person one hates, a persecutor.
G2190:2: One who is hostile to God, the cross, or the gospel; one in a relationship of enmity with God.
G2190:3: An evil power hostile to God's people, such as the devil or death.
G2233:1: One who goes first and guides, a leader, one at the head.
G2233:2: To think, to evaluate, to judge that…, to regard as.
G2240:1: Has already come, has arrived, came (perfect sense).
G2240:2: Will come, will arrive. Includes the coming of the Lord, the end, the day, and people.
G2246:1: The sun as a heavenly body; its rising and setting.
G2246:2: In the form ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου, the direction where the sun rises: the east.
G2246:3: The heat and scorching light of the sun.
G2296:1: To be astonished and filled with wonder at what one has seen or heard. The most typical use, where crowds, disciples, or Jesus marvel.
G2296:2: To feel admiration and praise toward a person or something powerful; a use with a note of commendation toward the object of wonder.
G2296:3: To be surprised and puzzled at something unexpected; used where one is told "do not be surprised", or is reproached for being surprised.
G2323:1: A person recovering from illness, affliction, a wound, or the troubling of an evil spirit, or being made to recover. In the active it means "to heal"; in the passive, "to be healed".
G2323:2: In Acts 17:25, God is said to be θεραπεύεται (served) by human hands. It states being given service and care, not recovery from illness.
G2342:1: A general use for wild animals, other creatures, venomous snakes, and other living things other than humans.
G2342:2: In Revelation, the "beast" portrayed as a powerful being rising from the sea or the earth; spoken of in connection with worship, the mark, and the image.
G2342:3: A figurative use comparing people to "beasts".
G2347:1: Pressure or suffering that a person receives from outside, such as persecution, want, or hardship. The most frequent use, as affliction that believers endure.
G2347:2: The unprecedented great affliction that comes before the last days; a use called the "great tribulation".
G2347:3: Pain and sorrow felt within a person, such as labor pains or an anguished heart.
G2364:3: "Daughters" as children of God, or as descendants of Aaron or Abraham.
G2364:4: "The daughter of Zion", a personification of a city or people.
G2374:1: The doorway or door of a house, room, prison, tomb, temple, and so on: ἡ θύρα κέκλεισται, κρούειν τὴν θύραν, λίθον τῇ θύρᾳ τοῦ μνημείου, αἱ θύραι τῆς φυλακῆς, etc.
G2374:2: Refers to the way in, as the door of the sheepfold (John 10) and the narrow door (Luke 13:24): ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα, διὰ τῆς στενῆς θύρας.
G2374:3: In the forms ἐγγύς ἐστιν ἐπὶ θύραις and ὁ κριτὴς πρὸ τῶν θυρῶν ἕστηκεν, says that something is close at hand.
G2374:4: In the form θύραν ἀνοίγειν, an opportunity for preaching and the work of the word is opened: θύρα μοι ἀνέῳγεν μεγάλη, ἤνοιξεν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν θύραν πίστεως, etc.
G2378:1: An offering of an animal or other item given to God; a ritual sacrifice.
G2378:2: The one sacrifice that Christ made of himself.
G2378:3: A spiritual offering to God, such as believers' lives, praise, service, and almsgiving.
G2390:1: To heal illness or a wound; to be cured.
G2390:2: To give restoration from sin and rebellion; to heal.
G2396:1: Directs attention to a person or thing in front of one, pointing it out.
G2396:2: Draws the listener's attention and stresses what is about to be said, or one's surprise.
G2409:1: One who serves God in the temple and offers sacrifices: Levitical priests, and also pagan priests.
G2409:2: The eternal priest after Melchizedek and his line, that is, the priesthood of Christ.
G2409:3: God's people and believers becoming priests to God.
G2411:1: The temple in Jerusalem and its precincts.
G2411:2: The temple of a pagan god (such as the temple of Artemis).
G2411:3: An adjective meaning "holy" (in a short predicate statement).
G2413:1: The whole temple area in Jerusalem (including courts, porticoes, and gates). Appears as the place where people teach, buy and sell, pray, and are arrested. Distinguished from ναός, which refers to the sanctuary itself.
G2413:2: An adjective use stating that a thing is set apart for God: "holy writings", etc.
G2425:1: Being sufficient for what is needed: ἱκανόν ἐστιν (that is enough), ἱκανὸν τῷ τοιούτῳ (enough for such a person).
G2425:2: The set expressions τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι (to satisfy the crowd) and τὸ ἱκανὸν λαβεῖν (to take security).
G2425:3: Number, amount, or degree that is considerable: ὄχλος ἱκανός (a fair crowd), λαμπάδες ἱκαναί, ἀργύρια ἱκανά, ἱκανοὶ κοιμῶνται (quite a few sleep), etc.
G2425:4: In the forms χρόνος／ἡμέραι／ἔτη ἱκανοί, says that a time is considerably long.
G2425:5: A person having the capacity or qualification for a task or work: οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς + infinitive／ἵνα (I am not fit to…), τίς ἱκανός (who is fit?), etc.
G2478:1: One with strength, a strong person, an angel, a city, a person, God. Includes the comparative (stronger).
G2478:2: Strength and intensity of wind, famine, voice, cry, consolation, and so on.
G2480:1: To be able or have strength to do something (often negated: "could not").
G2480:2: To be effective, to be valid, to hold good, to exert force.
G2480:3: To be healthy and strong; "those who are well".
G2511:1: To heal a serious skin disease (leprosy) and make clean, or to be made clean.
G2511:2: To wash vessels, bodies, or things clean, or to purify (with blood, etc.) as the law prescribes.
G2511:3: To cleanse sin, unrighteousness, conscience, or heart: cleansing through Christ's blood, washing with water, purification by faith.
G2511:4: To treat food or things as clean, to declare them clean.
G2513:1: Without impurity; ritually or materially clean, tidy.
G2513:2: A heart, conscience, or character that is pure, without stain or falseness.
G2513:3: Free of responsibility, innocent, as in "I am innocent of your blood".
G2513:4: Pure and unmixed, as of gold or linen.
G2523:1: Intransitive: to sit, take a seat, sit down. Includes sitting to teach, eat, or ride.
G2523:2: Transitive: to seat a person, or to appoint them and place them in a seat.
G2523:3: To take a seat that shows authority: the throne, the seat of judgment, God's right hand, the seat of glory. Appears in the forms ἐκ δεξιῶν／ἐν δεξιᾷ, ἐπὶ θρόνου, and ἐπὶ βήματος.
G2523:4: To remain seated, that is, to stay in one place.
G2537:1: What has not existed before, what has newly appeared, or what differs from the earlier: καινὴ διαθήκη, ὄνομα καινόν, ᾠδὴ καινή, καινὴ κτίσις, ἐντολὴ καινή, etc.
G2537:2: Says of clothing, wineskins, tombs, and the like that they are new, that is, not yet used.
G2537:3: In the form καινότερον. In Acts 17:21, it is said of people who seek "something newer".
G2556:1: Badness or wickedness as a quality, said of a noun or as a predicate; used of persons, thoughts, deeds, and things.
G2556:2: A noun use in the neuter (τὸ κακόν／κακά), κακοῦ, and so on, referring to moral evil, bad deeds, or bad matters themselves. Often set against the good (ἀγαθόν／καλόν).
G2556:3: Evil that appears as loss or harm done to others, or as misfortune or calamity that befalls oneself.
G2573:1: The manner of something being in good order: an act, state, or treatment. States quality or dignity, such as "well built", "ran well", "rule well".
G2573:2: States that a word spoken, an answer, or a remark is right and to the point; the "you are right" or "well said" type.
G2573:3: In the form καλῶς ποιεῖν, a set expression approving or valuing an act: "it was good of you to…", "it is fine to…".
G2673:1: To nullify or abolish the law, a promise, faith, a stumbling block, and the like.
G2673:2: To make powerless or destroy power, an enemy, death, the body of sin, rulers.
G2673:3: Prophecy, knowledge, what is partial, an old glory, and the like pass away or cease.
G2673:4: To be released or cut off from the law or from connection with Christ.
G2673:5: To make a piece of land useless by taking up its space.
G2730:1: A person or spirit takes up residence in a place: "settled in Nazareth", "an evil spirit enters and settles", "where Satan lives", etc.
G2730:2: With a participle, "those living in…": the inhabitants of a land or town: "those living in Jerusalem", "those who dwell on the earth".
G2730:3: God, Christ, the fullness of deity, and the like take up residence in a place or person and dwell there.
G2744:1: To boast or brag about a person, deed, status, or possession; includes pride based on one's own standing or human qualifications.
G2744:2: To boast with confidence and joy in God, Christ, the cross, or in suffering and weakness, or to take joy in it; accompanied by ἐν κυρίῳ / ἐν θεῷ / ἐν Χριστῷ and the like.
G2799:1: To cry with voice or tears: οἱ κλαίοντες ὡς μὴ κλαίοντες, ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς, κλαίειν μετὰ κλαιόντων, μὴ κλαῖε, etc.
G2799:2: Scenes of weeping in mourning for the dead or dying: tears at the tomb in John 11 and 20, Luke 7:13 and 8:52, Matt 2:18 (Rachel for her children), Mark 5:38–39, etc.
G2799:3: To lament sorrow, regret, announced judgment, or the destruction of a city or the world: κλαύσατε ὀλολύζοντες (Jas 5:1), πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε, ἔκλαυσεν ἐπ᾽ αὐτήν (Luke 19:41), the laments of Revelation 18, etc.
G2902:1: To seize and hold a person. In the form ἐκράτησαν αὐτόν, it appears in scenes of arrest (John's capture, Jesus' arrest, the apostles' detention).
G2902:2: To seize and grip a hand, foot, and the like; includes "taking by the hand" in healing and raising scenes.
G2902:3: To keep hold of teaching, tradition, confession, name, and the like without letting go.
G2902:4: To hold down a movement or activity and not let it be free (eyes held back, held by death, holding back the wind, retaining sins).
G2902:5: To achieve or seize a purpose or hope, overcoming obstacles. Acts 27:13 (where sailors thought they had gained their aim in the voyage) is the New Testament use.
G2917:1: God's judgment, a trial or verdict, the act of judging.
G2917:2: A guilty verdict, punishment, or blame received as the outcome of judgment.
G2917:3: A dispute or lawsuit between people.
G2917:4: God's decision and decree, the ordained judgment.
G2920:1: Judgment by God or Christ, especially the judgment of the last day. Appears in the form ἡμέρα κρίσεως and is spoken of as a judgment ending in a verdict of guilt and punishment.
G2920:2: The rightness that is the content of judgment, justice. Listed with ἔλεος and ἀγάπη as matters to be kept.
G2920:3: Judgment by a human court or tribunal.
G2920:4: κρίσις as an individual verdict, judgment, or decision. Said of human judgment, and of God's decisions (plural).
G2968:1: A small settlement as against a town: a village.
G3049:1: To think over a matter and arrive at an opinion, judgment, or conclusion: λογίζομαι γὰρ ὅτι (I reckon that…), ἐλογιζόμην ὡς νήπιος, ταῦτα λογίζεσθε (think on these things), etc.
G3049:2: To regard A as B, or for A to be regarded as B: λογιζέσθω ἄνθρωπος ὡς ὑπηρέτας, ἐλογίσθημεν ὡς πρόβατα, εἰς σπέρμα λογίζεται, εἰς οὐθὲν λογισθῆναι, etc.
G3049:3: Faith or wages are entered to an account as "righteousness" and the like: ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην, ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν, etc.
G3049:4: To count a person's sins and wrongs and hold them against them: οὐ λογίζεται τὸ κακόν, μὴ λογιζόμενος αὐτοῖς τὰ παραπτώματα, μὴ αὐτοῖς λογισθείη.
G3076:1: To grieve, lament, be pained at heart.
G3076:2: To make a person or the Spirit sad, to distress.
G3089:1: To loose what is tied, joined, or sealed: sandal straps (ἱμάς), a colt, an ox, seals (σφραγῖδες), wrappings (John 11:44), the bond of the tongue (Mark 7:35), etc.
G3089:2: To free a person or being from restraint, bondage, or detention: λύειν ἐκ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν, λυθῆναι ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσμοῦ, angels or Satan being released, loosing from chains (Acts 22:30), λέλυσαι ἀπὸ γυναικός, etc.
G3089:3: To tear down or break up what stands: a building, a dividing wall, all things, the law, Scripture, the Sabbath, a work: λύειν τὸν ναόν, τὸ μεσότοιχον λύσας, τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου, λυθῆναι ἡ γραφή, στοιχεῖα λυθήσεται, etc.
G3089:4: λύω used in Matt 16:19 and 18:18 in a pair with δέω (to bind): what is "loosed" on earth is stated as "loosed" in heaven. The content of the meaning is left to the context; here it is set apart as a formal usage.
G3089:5: An assembly or meeting ends and the people disperse. Acts 13:43 only.
G3107:1: A word that pronounces and states blessing and happiness before God for a person or their condition. Includes beatitude pronouncements of the form Μακάριοι οἱ….
G3107:2: Modifies God and states happiness as an attribute of God.
G3107:3: Used of things and matters rather than people, modifying a womb, a hope, and the like.
G3141:1: Testimony in court or public, and the witness that a person or God gives: ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ θεοῦ, ἡ μαρτυρία μου, τὴν μαρτυρίαν οὐ λαμβάνετε, ψευδομαρτυρίαι (Mark 14), ἡ μαρτυρία αὕτη ἀληθής, etc.
G3141:2: The evaluation or good name given by those around: μαρτυρίαν καλὴν ἔχειν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔξωθεν (1 Tim 3:7).
G3141:3: In the form ἡ μαρτυρία Ἰησοῦ (Χριστοῦ), refers to the testimony of (concerning, or by) Jesus. Rev 1:2, 1:9, 12:17, 19:10, 20:4.
G3144:1: A witness set up to establish the truth of an event or a statement: "by the mouth of two or three witnesses", etc.
G3144:2: A witness as eyewitness and testifier to events seen and heard (Jesus' resurrection, works, suffering).
G3144:3: One who was killed because of their testimony.
G3144:4: An expression calling God (or the listeners) as witness that one's words and thoughts are true.
G3162:1: A sword or dagger as a weapon; execution or battle by the sword.
G3162:2: The sword as what brings strife and killing rather than peace.
G3162:3: A symbol of the authority to punish that rulers bring upon wrongdoers.
G3162:4: A figure for the sword of the Spirit and the sharpness of God's word.
G3196:1: A part or organ of a person's body (hand, eye, tongue, etc.), and its function. Includes bodily members as the basis of the body metaphor.
G3196:2: Believers as members of Christ's body and members of one another.
G3313:1: A part that makes up a whole, or one of several divided portions: τρία μέρη (three parts), ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ μέρος, ἑνὸς ἑκάστου μέρους, μέρος τι (some part), etc.
G3313:2: The share allotted and given to someone: ἔχειν μέρος ἐν…／μετ᾽… (to have a share in…), τὸ ἐπιβάλλον μέρος (the share that falls to one), τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀπίστων, etc.
G3313:3: In the form τὰ μέρη + a place name or direction, refers to a region of land: τὰ μέρη Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος, τὰ μέρη τῆς Γαλιλαίας, etc.
G3313:4: One of two or more sides, or one party: τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ πλοίου (the right side of the boat), τὸ ἓν μέρος Σαδδουκαίων.
G3313:5: In the forms ἐκ μέρους／ἀπὸ μέρους (and μέρος τι), states that something is partial and does not cover the whole.
G3313:6: A set expression for speaking in distinct parts: κατὰ μέρος (one by one), ἀνὰ μέρος (in turn).
G3313:7: In the forms ἐν μέρει + genitive and ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει, limits the range of a matter: "in respect of…", "in this matter".
G3313:8: Refers to the field of a trade or business. Acts 19:27 only (in the context where the silversmith's work is exposed to disrepute).
G3340:1: To turn heart and way of life away from sin and deeds. Includes the call to repentance and its carrying out.
G3340:2: To express regret toward a person (a brother) and apologize.
G3383:1: In the form μήτε … μήτε …, lists several items, negating each. Used in prohibition, supposition, and negative sentences.
G3397:1: Small in size, amount, or degree. Modifies ζύμη, μέλος, ποίμνιον, δύναμις, and others; in the form μικρόν τι it states "a little".
G3397:2: Refers to a "little one" in terms of a person's status or importance: the form τῶν μικρῶν τούτων, and "small and great" paired with μεγάλος.
G3397:3: μικρόν used adverbially or as a noun, for a short time or soon. Appears in the forms ἔτι μικρόν, μετὰ μικρόν, and μικρὸν χρόνον.
G3397:4: With προελθών, states going on only a little farther.
G3404:1: To direct hostility or hatred toward a person or group: ὁ κόσμος ὑμᾶς μισεῖ, ὁ μισῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, οἱ μισοῦντες ἡμᾶς, the passive (ἔσεσθε μισούμενοι ὑπὸ πάντων), etc.
G3404:2: In contrast with ἀγαπάω, a way of speaking that chooses one and sets the other aside: τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει, οὐ μισεῖ τὸν πατέρα ἑαυτοῦ, ὁ μισῶν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ.
G3404:3: To loathe things other than people, such as evil, deeds, light, and impurity: ἐμίσησας ἀνομίαν, μισεῖς τὰ ἔργα τῶν Νικολαϊτῶν, μισεῖ τὸ φῶς, ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο ποιῶ, etc.
G3408:1: Reward from heaven or from God; receiving a reward.
G3408:2: Payment for one who has worked; wages.
G3408:3: Pay gained by unrighteousness; the reward of evil.
G3419:1: A place where the dead are buried. Refers to a tomb chamber cut in rock, or a burial ground: ἐν μνημείῳ ἔθηκεν, τὸ μνημεῖον (the tomb of Jesus or Lazarus), ἐκ τῶν μνημείων (from the tombs), etc.
G3419:2: Scenes of building and adorning the tombs of prophets and righteous people: οἰκοδομεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν προφητῶν, κοσμεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν δικαίων.
G3466:1: God's plan and saving truth that was hidden and has now been revealed.
G3466:2: The hidden meaning of a symbol in a vision, or a secret contained in a name.
G3466:3: Matters spoken by the Spirit that people cannot grasp.
G3483:1: An affirmative reply or agreement to a question or call.
G3483:2: Introduces an assertion or emphasis, as in "Truly, I say to you" and "Yes, I am coming".
G3483:3: The word "yes" itself, also mentioned as one of a pair (ναί／οὔ).
G3485:1: The main sanctuary of the Jerusalem temple. Appears as the place where the curtain is torn, incense is burned, and of which it is said, "destroy it and in three days I will raise it up".
G3485:2: A use in which the bodies or community of believers are described as the temple in which God dwells.
G3485:3: A temple to pagan gods, or a model of one.
G3485:4: God's temple in heaven. Appears in Revelation as the temple in a vision.
G3528:1: To conquer or overcome enemies, evil, the world, the beast, and so on.
G3528:2: In the promises to the churches in Revelation, the blessing given to "the one who conquers".
G3528:3: To win a dispute or a lawsuit when one's rightness is recognized.
G3618:1: To actually build a house, tower, city, synagogue, temple, tomb, and the like: οἰκοδομεῖν οἶκον／πύργον／οἰκίαν, οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες (the builders), the saying about rebuilding the temple (Matt 26:61 and elsewhere).
G3618:2: To support and strengthen the faith and growth of a person or community: ἡ ἀγάπη οἰκοδομεῖ, ἑαυτὸν／ἐκκλησίαν οἰκοδομεῖ, οἰκοδομεῖτε εἷς τὸν ἕνα, etc.
G3618:3: Using the image of building to build up the church, a work, a way of life: οἰκοδομήσω μου τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, οἰκοδομεῖσθε οἶκος πνευματικός, ἐπ᾽ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον οἰκοδομῶ, etc.
G3631:1: An alcoholic drink made from grapes: as a drink, a commodity, a medicine, or wedding wine. Includes the parable of new wine.
G3631:2: Wine as an apocalyptic figure: the cup of God's wrath, the wine of Babylon's immorality, and so on.
G3631:3: A context warning against being given to wine and drinking too much.
G3641:1: Small number or amount: οἱ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι (the workers are few), ὀλίγοι οἱ σῳζόμενοι, ὀλίγα ἰχθύδια, οἴνῳ ὀλίγῳ (a little wine), etc. Besides the adjective use, also used as a noun (ὀλίγοι "a few people", ὀλίγα "a few things").
G3641:2: In the forms ὀλίγον (adverb, accusative), πρὸς ὀλίγον, and πρὸς ὀλίγας ἡμέρας, states that time is short.
G3641:3: ὀλίγον states smallness of distance or degree: "a little (farther)", "only a little".
G3641:4: The negated form οὐκ ὀλίγος, "not a few", that is, "a considerable number, amount, or degree" (litotes).
G3641:5: In the forms ἐν ὀλίγῳ and δι᾽ ὀλίγων, to speak in few words (a way of writing a letter).
G3660:1: To swear by God, heaven, the temple, and the like, or to swear to something as a witness.
G3660:2: God swears and makes a promise or judgment certain.
G3664:1: Being the same as another in nature, manner, or kind. In the form ὅμοιος τινι, states that it is of the same kind as the thing compared.
G3664:2: A set use that introduces a parable: "the kingdom of heaven is like…", "… is like a person who…".
G3664:3: A use rhetorically asking "who is like…?", that is, there is nothing to compare.
G3664:4: A use describing the form, color, and appearance of what is seen in a vision as like something known (concentrated in Revelation).
G3668:1: An adverb showing that it is in the same manner or the same situation as what was said before: "likewise", "in the same way".
G3670:1: To confess Christ, God, or the Lord publicly before people; to express faith.
G3670:2: To state a fact or position plainly, admit, declare openly.
G3670:4: To promise on oath; to say what one has promised.
G3694:1: To follow after a person or thing, as in "follow after me" and "go after…"; also to go after someone.
